units.why: Says the update 'leaves undisturbed the 2023 default approach' that the Code of Academic Integrity covers AI; this sets the default fallback (P06) rather than a new rule.

units.passage: If an instructor wishes to permit certain uses of GAI tools or other AI resources, such uses must be set forth explicitly in the course syllabus and/or assignment instructions; otherwise, the default rules apply.
units.why: "such uses must be set forth explicitly in the course syllabus and/or assignment instructions; otherwise, the default rules apply" is a fallback rule when the syllabus is silent (P06).

units.passage: In the absence of explicit directions to the contrary from instructors, the following default rules apply at the University
units.why: "In the absence of explicit directions to the contrary from instructors, the following default rules apply at the University" states the fallback when instructors are silent, P06; it is a framing sentence for the rules below, so general scope.

units.passage: When no explicit guidance is given, GSU’s Disclosure Standards direct students to default to full disclosure of any AI use
units.why: "When no explicit guidance is given, GSU's Disclosure Standards direct students to default to full disclosure of any AI use" is a fallback when instructions are silent, P06 rather than P24.

units.passage: Don’t assume any AI use is acceptable.
units.why: "Don’t assume any AI use is acceptable" sets a default for silence: no assumption of permission. That is a fallback (P06), not the ask-first advice coded separately as P10.

units.passage: If the instructor does not provide guidance, students should cite content derived from AI tools using the style most closely resembling the course or department's general academic submission format.
units.policy: If the instructor does not provide guidance, students cite content derived from AI tools using the style most closely resembling the course or department's general academic submission format
units.why: 'If the instructor does not provide guidance, students should cite content derived from AI tools' sets what applies when the syllabus is silent, so P06 rather than P24: the point is the fallback, though it is a citation duty (should).

units.passage: Unless permission is explicitly granted, all assignments must be completed independently and without assistance from automated tools.
units.why: Option 2 sets the rule when no permission is given: "all assignments must be completed independently and without assistance from automated tools", a fallback ban, P06.

units.passage: AI generators/programs such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, Spinbot, Dall-E, etc. should not be used for any work for this class without explicit permission of the instructor and appropriate attribution.
units.why: The suggested disclaimer says AI tools "should not be used for any work for this class without explicit permission of the instructor and appropriate attribution", a silent-means-no rule; P06.

units.policy: AI-generated work is not acceptable unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator.
units.why: "AI-generated work ... is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator" sets a default ban absent explicit permission, which is the fallback rule (P06); the instructor authority is coded separately as P04.

units.why: The phrase "except as expressly permitted" means AI is banned unless the instructor says otherwise; the default when the syllabus is silent is prohibition. This fallback rule is P06; P01 is close but the document pairs the default with a required express permission.

units.fit_note: Also sets a default of no AI when the instructor is silent; P06 chosen over P01 because the key element is the written-consent condition.

units.passage: Absent a clear statement from a course instructor, use of or consultation with generative AI shall be treated analogously to assistance from another person.
units.policy: Absent a clear statement from a course instructor, use of or consultation with generative AI shall be treated analogously to assistance from another person.
units.why: "Absent a clear statement from a course instructor" opens the fallback default for when the instructor says nothing, so P06 is the right type. The content of the fallback (analogy to another person) is coded separately as P45.
units.fit_note: The fallback is not a ban: AI is treated like help from another person, which is allowed or not depending on Honor Code rules for such help.

units.passage: Unless otherwise specified, the use of Automated Writing Tools
units.policy: Unless otherwise specified, use of automated writing tools including ChatGPT and similar AI tools is strictly prohibited in the course, even when properly attributed.
units.why: Sample (UNH): "Unless otherwise specified" AI tools are strictly prohibited "even when properly attributed"; this states the fallback when the instructor specifies nothing, P06.
units.fit_note: Also says attribution does not cure the violation ("even when properly attributed").

units.passage: Using generative AI without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus
units.why: The quoted TCU policy says generative AI use 'without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus' is misconduct. AI is banned unless approved or stated in the syllabus, a fallback when unapproved, P06; P01 does not fit as syllabi may permit.
units.fit_note: Approval can be documented by instructor or syllabus.

units.passage: These policies should be clearly defined in the course syllabus and absent a clear syllabus statement use of or consultation with generative AI shall be treated similarly to assistance from another person or an uncited resource.
units.policy: Absent a clear syllabus statement, use of or consultation with generative AI shall be treated similarly to assistance from another person or an uncited resource.
units.why: "absent a clear syllabus statement" AI use "shall be treated similarly to assistance from another person or an uncited resource" is a fallback rule for silent syllabi (P06), chosen over P45 because the rule is triggered by silence.
units.fit_note: A: Also treats AI like help from another person or an uncited resource (P45); P06 does not capture the analogy. B: Fallback is an analogy to human help or uncited sources, not an outright ban.

units.passage: Otherwise, the default is that AI is not allowed during any stage of an assignment.
units.why: "Otherwise, the default is that AI is not allowed during any stage of an assignment" states the fallback when permission is absent, P06, must-not.

units.passage: Unpermitted assignments (i.e., any assignment lacking explicit AI permissions) must be entirely your own work, without AI tools.
units.why: 'Unpermitted assignments (i.e., any assignment lacking explicit AI permissions) must be entirely your own work, without AI tools' defines the fallback: no explicit permission means no AI; P06.
units.fit_note: Own-work requirement framed as a ban on AI tools for unpermitted assignments.

units.passage: Where no local guidance is provided, individuals may make their own decisions about how to use and disclose AI according to these guidelines.
units.why: The fallback when local guidance is silent is that "individuals may make their own decisions", not a default ban, so P06 with a note.
units.fit_note: Fallback is individual judgment under the guidelines, not a ban or blanket allowance.

units.passage: Any use outside of when permission is explicitly given will be considered academic dishonesty and a violation of the University of Illinois Student Code.
units.why: 'Any use outside of when permission is explicitly given will be considered academic dishonesty'; the fallback when permission is absent, P06.

units.passage: For all other assignments and tasks, students are expected to do their own work without the assistance of AI to generate or modify content or responses.
units.why: 'For all other assignments and tasks, students are expected to do their own work without the assistance of AI' is the rule for assignments that say nothing: P06.

units.passage: Submission of an assignment (e.g., term paper, software program, etc.) purchased from a private or commercial entity; or generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted.
units.policy: Submitting an assignment generated by AI is cheating unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted.
units.why: The sentence lists AI-generated submissions as cheating "unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted", so the default is a ban with explicit permission as the only exception. This is a fallback rule for silence, hence P06 rather than P01 (a flat ban) or P04 (no per-instructor choice is stated here).
units.fit_note: The text does not mention syllabus silence; it sets AI-generated work as prohibited unless explicitly permitted, which also overlaps P19.

units.passage: If a statement on the use of generative AI tools is not provided by an instructor, the use of such tools is permitted but must be disclosed.
units.policy: If an instructor does not provide a statement on generative AI tools, their use is permitted but must be disclosed.
units.why: "the use of such tools is permitted but must be disclosed" gives the fallback when no instructor statement exists: permitted with mandatory disclosure. P06 (fallback when silent), chosen over P24 because the point is the default.

units.passage: If you do not provide a statement on the use of generative AI tools, then the university permits students to use generative AI tools, but they must disclose all generative AI usage.
units.policy: If an instructor provides no statement on generative AI tools, the university permits students to use them but they must disclose all generative AI usage.
units.why: "the university permits students to use generative AI tools, but they must disclose all generative AI usage" is the university fallback when the syllabus is silent (P06); it also makes students disclose, but the fallback is the main point.

units.passage: Students may only use materials approved by their instructor when completing an assignment or exam.
units.why: 'Students may only use materials approved by their instructor when completing an assignment or exam' means unapproved resources, which would include AI, are not allowed. It is not AI-specific, so P06 (unless allowed, not permitted) is only a partial fit.
units.fit_note: Coder A (P06): The sentence does not mention AI or a silent syllabus; it limits all materials to those the instructor approves. Coder B (P04): Not AI-specific; it covers all materials, which includes AI tools by implication.

units.passage: students shall rely on their own mastery of the subject and not attempt to receive help in any way not explicitly approved by the instructor.
units.why: Students must "not attempt to receive help in any way not explicitly approved by the instructor" on individual assessments; a default that unapproved help is barred, which covers AI by the following sentence. P06 nearest.
units.fit_note: A general rule on unapproved help for individual assessments, not specific to a silent syllabus or to AI. / Covers outside help generally, not AI by name.

units.passage: For all other assignments, the use of AI tools is prohibited and constitutes unauthorized assistance under the Honor Code.
units.policy: For all other assignments, the use of AI tools is prohibited and constitutes unauthorized assistance under the Honor Code
units.why: 'For all other assignments, the use of AI tools is prohibited and constitutes unauthorized assistance': what applies when an assignment does not designate AI (fallback rule, P06).

units.passage: If you have not explicitly authorized use of generative AI in completion of an assignment, inform students that they should consider AI to be an unauthorized resource
units.why: 'inform students that they should consider AI to be an unauthorized resource' sets the fallback when an assignment does not authorize AI; P06 (rule when syllabus is silent) fits exactly.

units.passage: Unless specifically permitted by the instructor, students should assume generative AI is unauthorized.
units.why: 'Unless specifically permitted by the instructor, students should assume generative AI is unauthorized' is the fallback rule when permission is absent, P06.

units.passage: Unless I have provided express permission to use an outside resource, assume it is not permitted
units.why: 'Unless I have provided express permission to use an outside resource, assume it is not permitted' is the fallback when the syllabus does not authorize a resource; the template's list of resources includes AI, so P06.
units.fit_note: Covers any outside resource; AI is named only in the instructor's list of examples.

units.passage: Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools.
units.why: Option 2 continues "Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools", a fallback that applies when no permission was given, so P06.
